key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics while preserving strain energy density and fracture energy under changes in interaction scale.
engineering_relevance: The learned model enables continuum fracture predictions on domains far larger than atomistic simulations can practically resolve.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density under horizon rescaling.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain a consistent energy release rate across scales.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered the underlying nonlocal model; MD-based tests matched energy metrics within 3% and out-of-distribution peak forces within 6%, while a plate with 4,000× the training-specimen area exhibited branching fracture.
watch_item: The reported tests do not establish generalization to other materials or fracture regimes, so application-specific validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
